messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Export g.part1
parts:
GGIR in its current form cannot do this.
I am not sure how you would interpret ENMO at high resolution? I think ENMO only has meaning when averaged per time window of 1 second or longer.
If you are interest in high resolution data then you are probably better off deriving the auto-calibration coefficients with GGIR and then writing your own function to load, calibrate, and store the raw data in a format of your choice.
Best, Vincent


On Fri, 1 Mar 2019 at 12:41, <javier.le...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello everyone,

Needless to say that GGIR allows to export g.part 2, g.part 4 and g.part5. However, due to research requirements, I would need to access to full detailed calibrated ENMO raw accelerometry data, at a certain epoch length. In this sense, I don't know if I'm right but I suppose g.part1 could offers that information. So, I would like to enquire some information, if possible, about the way I could export all raw accelerometry data processed through g.part1.

Maybe my deduction is being wrong or my enquirement has an obvious solution but, anyway, I would really appreciate any clarification.

Kind regards,
Javier.
